Specify a duration between two dates as a quasi-identifier

Source: R/anon_risk.R
anon_quasi_duration.Rd

Describes a duration in days between two dates of each subject, banded, such as treatment duration from RFSTDTC to RFENDTC in SDTM dm, for use in anon_risk(). Durations are not changed by date offsetting (a subject's dates all move together), so they can single subjects out even when the other quasi-identifiers meet the target.

Usage

anon_quasi_duration(dataset, start, end, width = 7, name = "DURATION")

Arguments

dataset

Name of the dataset in the list passed to anon_risk().

start, end

Names of the columns holding the start and end dates: Date or POSIXct columns, or ISO 8601 text (only full dates count; partial dates give a missing duration).

width

Width of the bands of days, a positive number: the duration end - start in days becomes the lower bound of its band, as anon_band() does with bottom = 0.

name

Name of the resulting quasi-identifier.

Value

An object of class "anon_quasi_duration".

Details

Each subject's duration comes from its first row (in row order) with both dates. A subject without both dates has a missing duration, which is a value of its own. The duration can only be measured: anon_generalize() and anon_suppress() don't change dates, and changing them would break study days (--DY). anon_deidentify() reports it among the residual signals.

Examples

dm <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = c("a", "b", "c"),
  RFSTDTC = c("2014-01-02", "2014-02-10", "2014-03-01"),
  RFENDTC = c("2014-06-30", "2014-08-01", "2014-03-20")
)
anon_risk(dm, quasi = anon_quasi_duration("data", "RFSTDTC", "RFENDTC", width = 28), max_risk = 1/2)
#> Re-identification risk
#> ======================
#> 
#> Quasi-identifiers: DURATION 
#> Measured without a step's record of suppressed cells: blanked cells count as missing values
#> Subjects: 3 
#> Target: maximum risk 0.5 (groups of at least 2) 
#> Maximum risk: 1 (smallest group: 1)  Average risk: 0.6666667 
#> Unique subjects (group of 1): 1 
#> Subjects in groups smaller than 2: 1 (33.3%)
#> Meets target: no 
#> 
#> Drivers (`_without` columns: result if that variable alone were left out):
#>  variable n_values n_missing n_unique_without n_below_k_without min_k_without
#>  DURATION        2         0                0                 0             3
#>  avg_risk_without
#>         0.3333333
